name: ntfy
description: Simple HTTP-based pub-sub notification service. Send push notifications to your phone or desktop via scripts.
summary: ntfy v2.32.0 (released 2026-10-18, https://github.com/binwiederhier/ntfy/releases/tag/v2.32.0) is the latest release, adding the `Incremental: ?1` header (RFC 10036) on streaming subscriptions to prevent proxy buffering, and hardening experimental clustering so housekeeping jobs run only on the cluster leader. v2.31.1 fixed a critical database overload regression from v2.31.0 caused by `since=<message ID>` reconnects scanning entire topic histories, resolved by adding a new composite index. v2.30.0 introduced experimental multi-server clustering via a shared PostgreSQL database, SMTP LOGIN auth support, and attachment links in email notifications.

answers.What is the current license?: Apache 2.0 (server) and GPL-2.0 (client libraries); check repository for exact terms
answers.Is the project actively maintained?: Yes — multiple releases in October 2026 with active bug fixes and new features
answers.Does it support authentication and acces: Yes — user provisioning via auth-users config, admin API, token-based auth, and access control lists
answers.Is there a hosted cloud version availabl: Yes — ntfy.sh is the official hosted cloud version

breaking_excerpts: v2.31.1 changes message DB schema from version 16 to 17 (new index); downgrading to v2.31.0 or earlier requires manually resetting the schema version in the database.
v2.31.0 experimental clustering: node registry schema changed from version 1 to 2; downgrading a clustered server to v2.30.0 requires manually resetting schema_version.
v2.31.0: reconnect with since=<message ID> may now return a few duplicate messages published in the same second; scripts not using ntfy apps must deduplicate by ID.

alternatives.name: Pushover
alternatives.review: Paid SaaS, simple API, iOS/Android apps.

alternatives.name: Gotify
alternatives.review: Self-hosted only, real-time push via WebSocket.

alternatives.name: Apprise
alternatives.review: Apprise is a powerful open-source notification library supporting 80+ services but is a library/CLI tool rather than a standalone pub-sub server.

alternatives.name: Pushbullet
alternatives.review: Pushbullet provides cloud-hosted cross-device notifications with file sharing but has a restrictive free tier and is a closed-source commercial product.

alternatives.name: Bark
alternatives.review: Bark is a lightweight open-source iOS push notification tool that is simpler to use than ntfy but is Apple-only with no native Android support.
